spans.s: 2. श॑म् ind. (g. चादि and स्वर्-आदि) auspiciously, fortunately, happily, well (frequently used in the Veda, rarely in later language; often to be translated by a subst., esp. in the frequent phrase शं॑ योः॑ or शं॑ च यो॑श् च, ‘happiness and welfare’, sometimes joined with the verbs भू, अस्, कृ, दा, वह्, या, sometimes occurring without any verb; with dat. or gen. [cf. Pāṇ. ii, 3, 73, Sch.]; in some cases corresponding to an adj., e.g. शं तद् अस्मै, that is pleasant to him), RV.; &c.

1. सम् or स्तम् cl. 1. P. समति or स्तमति, to be disturbed (accord. to some ‘to be undisturbed’; cf. √ शम्), Dhātup. xix, 82;
 cl. 10. P. समयति or स्तमयति, to be agitated or disturbed, Vop.
